clue.text: Vehicle needs protection at the front

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
a guard is a form of protection

explanation.surface: Advice that a vehicle should carry some protection on its nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adverbial: to be 'in the vanguard' is to be at the front, and the noun is used loosely here.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading part of an army or movement is its vanguard, the position furthest forward.

clue.text: One member of the family currently at Oxford

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
sis is short for sister, one member of a family

explanation.surface: A relative of yours is studying at Oxford University right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' puns on current: the Isis is the name used for the River Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the River Thames passing through Oxford is traditionally given this name, so it is the current there.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the two words are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that choking has been omitted from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IS and LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle someone is to choke or suffocate them, cutting off breath.

clue.text: Post on ship or shore for a sailor

definitions.text: Post on ship or shore for a sailor

parts.words: Post on ship or shore for a sailor
parts.note: describes a short sturdy post, found on a deck or a quayside, round which a sailor makes fast a mooring rope

explanation.surface: A sailor's posting could be at sea or ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job or a posting for a sailor; it is a literal post that ropes are tied to.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring post on a quay or a ship's deck is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Teams in the markets for left-wingers

indicators.note: in tells us the teams are placed inside the word for markets

parts.note: marts are markets
an XI is a team of eleven players, so teams are XIs

explanation.surface: Teams of traders in the markets are said to be on the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football side is an eleven, written XI, so the plural is XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Karl Marx's communist theory sit on the far left of politics.

parts.note: in the biblical parable a father kills the best-fed young animal for a feast when his wayward son comes home; fare means food, not a ticket price

explanation.surface: What the prodigal son paid for his ticket home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return fare' suggests a travel ticket; here fare is the meal served to celebrate the son's return.
explanation.definitionFit: In Luke's gospel the father orders a fattened young animal killed for the homecoming feast, so it is the food eaten.

clue.text: I want a free, democratic island

indicators.note: free signals the letters are set loose to form a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea for a free and democratic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges I WANT A.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-governing island off the Chinese coast holds multiparty elections, making it a democratic island.

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight or battle

explanation.surface: A shrill-sounding fight by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice above the normal male range is described this way, so it is high-pitched.

clue.text: Mount framing an artist in his element

indicators.note: in places the artist inside the word for his element

parts.note: an artist's element, the field he is at home in, is art
an gives A
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A mountain surrounding a painter who is in his element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' plays on a mount framing a picture; it serves only the surface. This is the mountain where Noah's ark came to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey is the peak where the ark is said to have landed.

definitions.meaning: to egg someone on is to urge or encourage them
food that can be poached, among other ways of cooking

explanation.surface: Someone encourages poaching of game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poaching' suggests illegal hunting; it is a way of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Egging someone on means urging them, and hen's ova are classic poaching material.

clue.text: Boy going to school in Suffolk

parts.note: Felix is a boy's name
Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A lad heading off to boarding school in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a well-known English private school; the answer is a port town on the Suffolk coast in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This port town lies on the coast of Suffolk, so it is a place found in that county.

indicators.note: follow tells us the word for lots comes after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: ample means plenty, lots

explanation.surface: Many people come after a second examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like a noun subject; it stands for plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: To try out a small portion of something is to test it.

definitions.meaning: a pale shade of blue-violet named after a flower
a small edible sea snail, also called a winkle

explanation.surface: A sad shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' reads as sad; it is the colour, named after the flowering plant of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lavender-blue colour and an edible sea snail.

indicators.note: out tells us the letters of these words are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house that is let to tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IS RENTED. 'Dwelling' is an adjective: living in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dwelling in a place is living there, an adjectival sense of the word.

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience
the house, street and town telling the post where to deliver

explanation.surface: A speech written out on the back of an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal talk and the location details written on mail.

parts.note: surgical operations end with a wound being sewn closed using threaded loops

explanation.surface: Partners who team up in business operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operations' suggests business or military activity; it is surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons close wounds with sutures, loops of thread that hold skin together.

indicators.note: reparations means repairs, so the letters are remade into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guilty person who has made amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reparations' rearranges HAS MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling embarrassed and guilty about one's conduct is the sense of this adjective.

parts.note: even means calm, as in an even temper
a tide is a flow of sea water

explanation.surface: Still water at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, the time of dusk.

clue.text: Opposed to profit in a way

indicators.note: in tells us the word for profit is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone who in some way objects to making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'somewhat'; it is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being opposed to it.

clue.text: An automatic grill should do it

definitions.meaning: an automatic pistol made by the American gunmaker of that name
a grill toasts food until it turns a darker colour

explanation.surface: An automatic grill ought to do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'automatic' looks like a feature of the grill; it is a self-loading gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning is a make of automatic pistol and also what grilling does to toast.

indicators.note: form of says a new shape is made from the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A highly unusual kind of arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ARREST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of rare means least common, hence most unusual.

indicators.note: back means the word for lie is turned round

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
fed means having eaten

explanation.surface: Lying back after a meal, then getting hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie back' looks like resting after a meal, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To biff someone is to hit them, so biffed means whacked.

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unjustly blamed for a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges BLAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after an old London asylum, means a scene of chaos and uproar.

parts.note: issue means children, so this is the child of one's own child

explanation.surface: The matter of having children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a matter or problem; it means descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A son or daughter's child is the issue born to one's offspring.

parts.note: a cut is a stroke, as in cricket
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A smart shot sent towards a fielding position.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a cut is a stroke and point is a fielding position, which is the surface trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or clever, especially in American usage.

definitions.meaning: in carpentry, to shape the end of a moulding so it fits snugly against another
a long ceremonial cape worn by priests

explanation.surface: Trim a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a priest's long vestment and, in joinery, to cut a piece to fit.

clue.text: Operatic heroine that is at heart betrayed

indicators.note: at heart places the word for betrayed in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is
sold, as in sold out, means betrayed

explanation.surface: An opera heroine who is betrayed deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLD goes inside I.E., the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

indicators.note: by means the letter for eastern is placed beside the word for impressed

parts.note: stamped means impressed, as a mark pressed in

explanation.surface: Someone impressed by eastern flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' reads as admiring; it means marked by pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a panicked rushing flight of a herd.
